person_made_it: Eric's own board format from the brief (Board > Group > Item, Owner, Status chips Done / Working on it / Stuck / Not started, latest update, Definition of Done) and his event naming 'Event @ Venue (Day, time)', which he builds himself on the first screen; Gordon's line 'I have ideas. You have follow-through.' closes it.
emcee_who_is_speaking: Darby, openly, for Gordon; the crew speak in their own latest-update lines; an ElevenLabs announcer voice (Marc) calls 'crew is standing by' and 'you are go for launch'; Gordon is a lightbulb named Ideas, not a likeness.
what_time_of_day_is_this_room: dusk in a walnut mission-control room, then launch night under stage lights.
did_the_click_pay_me: assigning snaps a card onto the board (magnetic click, 'Perfect match' sparkle when the specialty fits), the crew card bobs and types with a typing loop, Stuck arrives with a soft marimba 'uh oh' and a one-tap choice that pops it loose, each Done is a stamp and chime with a chip flip and confetti burst; signing the Definition of Done launches the show: rumble, the announcer, four banks of light clunking on, his event name on the banner, fanfare and applause.
works_for_the_recipient: Played to the end with real input in WebKit 390x844 (tap, tap), Chromium 1920x1080 (two mouse drags, then clicks) and Chromium 2560x1440 (keyboard only: arrows, 1 to 5, U, Enter); 0 page errors, no sideways scroll; PC is a two-column console that scales its type and art with the width; JS off shows the board as a table, the crew, the lines and the link back.
taught_me_something: an Executive Producer's real job, shown as play: assign, unblock with a decision only you can make, and sign off the Definition of Done.
told_me_the_truth: no Monday.com branding, only the format and the four status words; event, venue and day are Eric's picks from labeled choices, not a claimed real event; crew roles are short and generic; the boys and Crystal are not in this one.
weakest: The stuck questions are scripted, the same three every run, and a fast player can finish the board in under a minute; a pool of rotating calls and a second wave tied to his choices would keep repeat runs fresh.
